chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) did not see a problem with al-'azl (coitus interruptus).
So everything from which Allah took the covenant, it comes out.
Even if it be upon a solid rock.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for the permissibility of coitus interruptus in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) validates coitus interruptus (al-'azl) by interpreting the Covenant verse (7:172) as establishing a principle of 'exit' (kharuj) for anything from which a pledge was taken. This juristic reasoning suggests that since the potential progeny was extracted from Adam's loins, the seed can similarly be expelled without nullifying the divine covenant of potential life, a view reflecting the early Shia emphasis on natural signs in legal derivation.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Al Haza’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> did not see a problem with the coitus interruptus.

So heasws recited this Verse [7:172] And when your Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify against their own souls: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes!. Thus, everything which Allahazwj Took the Covenant from it, so it comes out,
even though it may be upon a solid rock’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman al- Fiaddhdha’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, did not consider withdrawing before semen discharge as unlawful

and he (the Imam) read this verse, ‘When your Lord took of children of Adam from their backs their offspring and made them to bear witness for their souls about the question, “Am I not your Lord?” They replied, “Yes, You are our Lord.’” [7:171] Therefore, everything from which Allah has taken a covenant comes out
even if it is on a blind (solid) rock.’”
